main_body: Conical thatched hut: a large beehive thatch roof (rows 2-55) over a short clay wall (rows 56-77) with an arched doorway.
top_band: The thatch roof is a sloped top surface, lightest at the upper left (#d8bb68/#bc9a45), running from the apex at row 2 to the eave at about row 55 in banded courses. Below it the wall face is mid-brown.
evidence: The roof reads as a foreshortened cone slope seen from above, with an overhanging eave. A dark thatch edge at rows 53-56 casts shade onto the wall top. The wall below is a separate vertical face with a tone step, and its stone-grey base is also a distinct band. The door is inset, with a dark frame and an interior shadow, rather than painted flat. Roof and wall both satisfy the building contract, as in the reference houses where the roof is the visible top surface.

style.evidence: The thatch uses about 6 brown-gold steps, with per-course dark gaps and highlight dashes that give a straw texture. The wall carries plank or clay streaks, speckle and a grey stone base. The outline is a dark brown tinted to the material (7% neutral dark edge pixels, matching the references). Only 31 distinct colours and a median of 8 per tile are below both references (11 and 18), and flat-fill coverage is 12%, mostly the dark door interior. The thatch courses are fairly repetitive. Overall it holds up next to the references without looking sticker-like.
